title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial resumes after jurors visit crime scene
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Jurors visited Lindsay Clancy's former home in Duxbury and other key locations ahead of courtroom proceedings.
Lindsay Clancy, accused of killing her three children, is using an insanity defense citing postpartum mental illness.
Testimony from emergency personnel described the chaotic scene at Clancy's home the night of the murders.

title: Jarren Duran’s latest incident with Red Sox includes bizarre outburst involving Willson Contreras
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Jarren Duran had an outburst during a Red Sox game in Sacramento involving teammate Willson Contreras.
The incident followed Duran's flyout with runners on base, resulting in frustrations in the dugout.
Both Duran and manager Chad Tracy downplayed the incident, attributing Duran's reaction to self-criticism.

title: This provocative PETA protest at the Maine Lobster Festival is going viral
author: John Waller
bullets: PETA sent a nearly nude woman painted as a lobster to protest the Maine Lobster Festival in Rockland.
A PETA post about the protest on X has over 18 million views and nearly 4,000 reposts.
Festival organizers defend the event as a celebration of Maine's lobster industry with traditional methods.

title: This beloved Chinese restaurant is closing its doors after 54 years
author: John Waller
bullets: Lo Kai Restaurant & Lounge in Dracut announced it will permanently close on August 8, 2026.
The restaurant, a community staple since 1972, cited 'a number of factors' for its closure decision.
Local patrons shared memories on social media following the announcement, highlighting Lo Kai's impact.

title: 7 must-see artists at Newport Jazz Fest this weekend
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Newport Jazz Fest features artists like Herbie Hancock, Flea, Lake Street Dive, Jon Batiste, and Anoushka Shankar.
Herbie Hancock, a jazz fusion pioneer with 14 Grammys, will perform on Sunday at the festival.
Newport Jazz Fest runs from July 31 to August 2 at Fort Adams with a diverse lineup of performers.

title: Have Mass. farms seen an increase in sales due to cyclospora fears? It’s a mixed bag.
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Massachusetts farms experience mixed sales effects amid national cyclospora outbreak; some sell more produce, while others field safety questions.
Hutchins Farm in Concord increases lettuce picking by 50% due to higher demand linked to customer safety awareness.
Kimballs Fruit Farm in Pepperell sees general sales surge at farmers markets, doubling some products compared to last month.

title: How should the Red Sox approach the trade deadline?
author: Trevor Hass
bullets: The Red Sox have won 20 of their last 23 games, nearing playoff contention.
Chief Baseball Officer Craig Breslow might consider trading outfielders for infield or bullpen upgrades.
Mets reliever Luke Weaver is a potential option to strengthen the Red Sox bullpen.

title: After homicide ruling, Boston councilor wants officers involved in South Bay jail death placed on leave
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Boston City Councilor Miniard Culpepper calls for administrative leave for officers involved in Shacoby Kenny's death at South Bay jail.
State medical examiner rules Shacoby Kenny's death a homicide, prompting renewed calls for independent oversight of correctional facilities.
Attorney General Andrea Campbell's office leads a criminal investigation into Kenny's death, with no charges announced yet.

title: Norwood Hospital moves closer to being acquired through eminent domain
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Massachusetts Senate approved a bill for eminent domain seizure of Norwood Hospital property for nonprofit ownership.
The hospital has been closed since 2020 due to flood damage; construction halted when Steward Health Care filed for bankruptcy.
The bill allows Massachusetts to start eminent domain by November 1, shifting property control to a nonprofit health entity.

title: Patriots rookie Eli Raridon is looking like a potential Day 1 contributor
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Eli Raridon, Patriots' 2026 third-round pick, is stepping up in training camp as a potential immediate contributor.
With tight end Julian Hill injured, Raridon has earned reps behind starter Hunter Henry in the tight-end lineup.
Coach Mike Vrabel praises Raridon for adapting to the NFL speed, noting his athleticism and eagerness to learn.
